chapters.title: Welcome, and a hard two weeks

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Welcome, everyone. I'm so happy to be back — and I'm also extremely tired. We just finished two weeks of SCIM, and it was intense.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And then, on the very first day, they were like, "You know what? I realize I have too much to do, and I won't be able to help." And then I had to do the whole thing myself — well, not everything, but most of it. And then they were like, "Can you be in a private group as a trainee with another two people?"

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And then I just kept going and finished the whole thing. But I complained every single day. My poor, beautiful wife was like, "Could you just shut up and keep doing the work?" She didn't say it, but I could feel it — she's too kind to say it. And then one day she comes and she's like, "If you knew you were that busy, why did you ask to be a trainee too?" And I said, "I didn't ask — they invited me, and I said yes. They asked me for a favor." And then she said, "Okay."

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Why am I telling you this? First, because I'm very sleepy. Second, because that's practice. A regular practice is like that.

chapters.title: Practice during hard times, and what's coming

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: A lot of us, in October, are going through a big thing. And things are going to start happening, if they haven't started already. And you will be complaining — you will be saying, "This seed system is just crap, it doesn't work." But I promise that if you keep going, you will get results. What is going to happen in October is a big, big thing. It's a tremendous amount of good seeds that you will get — it will be ripening for you, and at the same time you will be planting them.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And that cleans the pipes. You will be heating the pipes. And that will stir all the mold and dirt that is inside the pipes. And things will come out. And after all the dirtiness — the mold — everything comes out, cleaner and more pure water will come from those pipes. And we have talked about this before.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: So just be ready. And if you feel like you need to complain, do it — with people inside your community, your sangha. If you have a teacher, look for your teacher's help. But always come back to remember that whatever you're going through, whatever you're going to experience, is coming from your mental seeds. And it is impermanent. Which is the whole topic of this level — how impermanent things are.

chapters.title: Proofs of past and future lives

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: We had a previous life before this, right? Classics Course 4 — now we have to call them classics courses. Right. The proofs of future and past lives, pretty much. A moment of mind can only come from a previous moment of mind — which logically implies that the first moment of mind in this life came from a previous moment of mind, a previous life.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And that is important, because the meditation that Tim and I are bringing you today — and the next days — relates to how different elements in our lives may have come from previous lives, and how those moments have led us here, today, to this moment, and how that will impact our future enlightenment. So it's very related to what is going to happen in October. Very. That's why Geshe Michael led those meditations the way he did in Malaysia.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: So what we're going to do today is think of important teachers that we had before our twelfth year — six years, or five. It doesn't matter — before twelve, let's say.

chapters.title: Where our early teachers come from

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: And it doesn't have to be school teachers — any kind of teacher. We're going to think about how those teachers taught us something that today is relevant for our practice.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Like, I had a teacher — a Spanish teacher — that I really hated.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Yeah, as a language, yeah. He was so tough with orthography and grammar and all those things that I hate, actually. Eventually, I ended up liking that teacher, and I learned a lot. Before him, I wouldn't care about those things. And after him, I still don't care — but I became good at it, every day, for my translations of the ancient classics. And I would never have imagined that I would be doing this.

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Where did that teacher come from? Well, the idea is that those early teachers, at least, come from previous lives — from the seeds of previous lives. So in this meditation, what we're going to try to do is figure out: what seed could I have planted in my previous life to see a particular teacher that impacted my life?

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: It could be that you're faking, or making up a story in your mind. But you've got to think about where that faking — where that mental image — is coming from too. So maybe it's not as fake as we think it is.

chapters.title: A KitKat and the Lion's Dance

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: For a KitKat — I can give one of these KitKats, right? Cool. In what other meditation do we do something similar?

paragraphs.speaker: Brian Mendoza
paragraphs.text: Yes. Yay — the Lion's Dance! Very similar, right? So if you already know the Lion's Dance meditation, you should be very familiar with today's meditation too. Only, in this one we're not so actively focused on the emptiness of the whole process — but just try to relate how it is coming from a previous life. And to be honest, it's very, very close to what we're learning in this level. It's crazy how the coincidence lines up — so this coincidence is quite beautiful.
